problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡(4x+{30}^{∘})=0
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a+n\cdot {45}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[{0}^{∘},{45}^{∘}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
worked_solution:
The given equation is equivalent to 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x+{30}^{∘})=0.
$$

So, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+{30}^{∘} & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & ={90}^{∘}-{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ 4x & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={15}^{∘}+n\cdot {45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a={15}^{∘}.$
